bundles.evidenceText: then the quantum field is the substance
bundles.rationale: The proposition is that material reality may consist of a single spacetime-pervading quantum-field substance. It can remain true whether actual infinities are impossible, beginningless succession can terminate, or an impersonal cause can originate a universe, so it has no route contact. The nearest candidate, attack on the pro central bridge, is excluded because the move neither asserts a beginningless past nor disputes the actual-infinite inference.

bundles.evidenceText: a beginningless uh series of events in time would entail an actually infinite number of past events
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that a beginningless past entails an actual infinity, that such an infinity cannot exist, and therefore that the temporal series and universe began. This directly supports the pro central bridge and cannot remain true without increasing that bridge's credibility. The pro actual-infinite subsidiary is excluded because the move mentions counterintuitive situations only generally rather than making a Hilbert-style concrete scenario its specific inference.

bundles.evidenceText: it's not quite clear to me that that's enough to say that it couldn't exist
bundles.rationale: The proposition is that Hilbert's Hotel may be strange while its unusual behavior is insufficient to establish metaphysical impossibility. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary bridge claiming that Hilbert-style scenarios reveal an actual infinite to be impossible, and its truth decreases that bridge's credibility. Support for the parallel con subsidiary is excluded by nearest exclusion because the move is framed as a direct rebuttal of the pro inference.

bundles.evidenceText: it will either happen from eternity or not at all
bundles.rationale: The move argues that an impersonal indeterministic or metastable source cannot plausibly originate the universe at one particular time, because it would produce its effect eternally or not at all. This directly attacks the con subsidiary bridge that such an impersonal cause could originate a first universe, and cannot remain true without reducing that bridge's credibility. Support for the pro personal-cause subsidiary is excluded as the nearest competitor because the move's operative inference directly refutes the proposed impersonal alternative despite also endorsing a personal explanation.
